solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wood topped with black slate

indicators.note: in a down clue the wood has the black letter placed on top of it, so that letter comes first

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
ash is a kind of timber

explanation.surface: A piece of timber with a dark stone covering laid on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate someone is to criticise them harshly, which is also what giving them a verbal attack means.

clue.text: Obstructed and unable to escape from the pit, we hear?

indicators.note: says the word meant is only heard, so a word sounding like it goes in the grid

parts.words: unable to escape from the pit
parts.note: the pit is hell, and a soul condemned there forever is damned

explanation.surface: Someone stuck and trapped down a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pit' is not a mine but the bottomless pit of hell; the damned sound almost exactly like a river that has been held back by a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A river that has been blocked by a barrier has been obstructed, the past tense matching.

clue.text: Catch coming from writer after start of story

indicators.note: puts the pen part behind the opening letter in the answer
asks for only the opening letter of the word story

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen, so it stands for a writer

explanation.surface: A good tale catches a reader once its author gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: SNIB is a Scottish word for a door latch.
explanation.definitionFit: A snib is a small bolt or fastening, a kind of latch that keeps a door shut.

clue.text: Untidy person with a bit of a neck

definitions.meaning: the nape, the back part of the neck by which an animal can be lifted

explanation.surface: A messy individual with part of a throat on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Scruff is both an informal word for a slovenly person and the name for the back of the neck.

clue.text: Proper greedy, eating last bit of supper

indicators.note: one piece takes another inside it, as a mouth takes in food

parts.note: piggish means greedy, like a pig at its trough

indicators.note: asks for only the final letter of the word supper

explanation.surface: A properly greedy person tucks into the end of their evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proper greedy' reads as slang for 'very greedy', but 'Proper' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excessively prim and concerned with correctness is self-righteously proper in manner.

clue.text: I con lass so wickedly in a holy letter

indicators.note: acting wickedly, the letters of these words are twisted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A rogue confesses to tricking a girl in a wicked way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to the Colossians is a letter of St Paul found in the New Testament.

clue.text: Fuel Norm needs to get a couple of females home

parts.note: par in golf is the expected standard, the norm
F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A man called Norm has to bring two women back to his house.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is kerosene, a lamp and heater oil burned as a fuel.

clue.text: Loud diatribe can be frightening

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical marking for loud
an earful is a long angry telling-off

explanation.surface: A noisy rant can be scary.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearful can mean causing fear, so a fearful sight is a terrifying one.

clue.text: Bottle supplied by garage apprentice?

parts.note: a garage is where a car is kept, so the building suggests its occupant
a boy is a young trainee or lad learning a trade

explanation.surface: A bottle provided by a youngster training at a motor workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A carboy is a large rounded glass or plastic bottle, often cased, for holding liquids.

clue.text: That man joining salvationists must follow a religious doctrine

indicators.note: the joined pieces come after the single letter in the answer

parts.note: him is the pronoun for that man
SA is the Salvation Army

explanation.surface: A man who joins the Salvation Army has to adopt its creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahimsa is the Hindu, Jain and Buddhist principle of non-violence towards all living things.

clue.text: Club unhappy about admitting BBC boss?

indicators.note: the sad word lets the boss's letters into it

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
DG is the Director-General, head of the BBC
on means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A sports club is upset at letting in the head of the broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC is Britain's public broadcaster, run by a Director-General.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a heavy club used as a weapon.

clue.text: One has unusual feel for this old book

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the letters is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: Someone takes an odd liking to a vintage volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' scrambles FEEL with FOR THIS OLD; 'One has' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord of the Flies is William Golding's 1954 novel about stranded schoolboys.

clue.text: Get rid of well-read old boy to start with

indicators.note: places the former pupil's letters at the beginning

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
literate can mean well-read and educated

explanation.surface: A former pupil who is cultured has to eliminate something first.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out completely, to destroy all trace of.

clue.text: Cool river for animal who'll like it?

parts.note: hip means fashionable, cool
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A chilly stream is just right for a creature that enjoys one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to the 'Cool river' itself: a river horse would enjoy such a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus spends its days wallowing in rivers, so it would enjoy a cool one.

clue.text: Tramp left in seedy home

indicators.note: the side's letter sits inside the seed case

parts.note: a pod is the case where seeds live

explanation.surface: A vagrant abandoned in squalid lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seedy' suggests shabby, but here it means 'containing seeds'.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod is to walk heavily and slowly, the same as to tramp along.

clue.text: US actress, one overtaken by our Diana over time?

indicators.note: in a down clue this piece sits above the time word
the British name engulfs the single digit

parts.note: Diana Dors was a British film actress, hence 'our'
I is the Roman numeral for one
a day is a span of time

explanation.surface: An American star is eclipsed in time by a home-grown one.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana Dors was a 1950s British screen star.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Day was a Hollywood singer and film star of the 1950s and 60s.

clue.text: Delight in the French pet?

parts.note: la is the French for 'the' (feminine)
a pup is a young dog kept as a pet

explanation.surface: Taking pleasure in a French family's dog.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up something is to enjoy it eagerly, to relish it.

clue.text: Introduce walk, having grabbed man on field

indicators.note: the walking word holds the official inside itself

parts.note: to pace is to walk
the ref, or referee, officiates on the pitch

explanation.surface: A stroll interrupted by grabbing a player from the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To preface something is to introduce it with opening remarks.

clue.text: Deception in house, a sign of something wrong

parts.note: a cross, X, marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: Trickery at home, betraying that something is amiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is a deliberate trick or fraud meant to deceive.

clue.text: Come, having got a word and its anagram, to show

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Come, having got a word and its anagram, to show (4,2,4,4)', gives TURN UP (come) + ONES/NOSE (word and anagram) but no definition of the phrase's sense of disdain; it looks cut short and no scan or search gives the rest.
annotationWithheld.clue: Come, having got a word and its anagram, to show

clue.text: Refined stuff that could have poisoned Abraham?

definitions.text: stuff that could have poisoned Abraham?
definitions.meaning: Abraham came from the city of Ur

explanation.surface: A cultured poison that might have finished off the patriarch.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Abraham set out from Ur of the Chaldees; bane is an old word for poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means elegant and smoothly courteous, as a refined person is.

clue.text: New monk in number overcoming wickedness

indicators.note: in a down clue the number piece sits on top of the wickedness

parts.note: vice means wickedness

explanation.surface: A monk in the ranks resisting sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a probationer in a religious order, a newly entered monk or nun.

clue.text: Angry local, one of two being horizontal at Anfield?

definitions.text: one of two being horizontal at Anfield?

parts.note: cross means angry
a local is a neighbourhood pub, a bar

explanation.surface: An irate drinker lying flat out at a football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Anfield is Liverpool FC's football ground; each of its two goals has a horizontal bar across the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbar is the horizontal bar joining a goal's two uprights; a pitch has two.

clue.text: Girl no good in what is predominantly male sport

indicators.note: says the good letter is dropped from the sport

parts.note: rugby is mostly played by men

explanation.surface: A woman who is useless at a game mostly played by men.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Notice trade going to pot around five

indicators.note: the scrambled business word is placed round the numeral
going to ruin, so the letters fall into disorder

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Commerce collapsing at about five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to pot' turns TRADE into ADERT, which goes around V.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a public notice promoting something.

clue.text: Revolutionary losing heart gets to falter

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a rebel is a revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel who loses courage begins to waver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes B, the centre of REBEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger or lose one's balance, to falter.

clue.text: Struggle making descent

definitions.meaning: to make a great effort, to struggle
a line of ancestry or breed

explanation.surface: Fighting hard while climbing down.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain means both to exert oneself to the utmost and a lineage or stock of descent.

clue.text: In trousers torn apart reportedly

indicators.note: signals that the word is only heard, so a soundalike goes in the grid

parts.note: a wall that has been breached has been broken through

explanation.surface: Someone in trousers ripped to pieces, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: A boy was breeched when he first got breeches, i.e. trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: To be breeched is to be dressed in breeches, an old word for trousers.
